pageSections.title: Predict remaining life using information available at prediction time
pageSections.description: A battery model needs chronological testing, deployable predictors, leakage screening, a simple baseline, and error measures tied to maintenance decisions.
pageSections.context: Refract's Stats workflow implements this sequence for its primary battery remaining-useful-life demonstration.

items.label: Profile
items.title: Profile each column
items.body: Measure missingness, ranges, distributions, and relationships before assigning predictors or targets.

items.label: Audit
items.title: Audit predictor timing
items.body: Identify when each signal becomes available and remove variables that contain future-cycle or target-derived information.

items.label: Split
items.title: Respect chronology
items.body: Train on earlier observations and evaluate on later observations that resemble the deployment decision.

items.label: Baseline
items.title: Establish a mean baseline
items.body: Measure how much error a constant prediction produces before adding model complexity.

items.label: Compare
items.title: Compare models
items.body: Evaluate Linear Regression and Random Forest with the same split, predictors, and MAE, RMSE, and R² calculations.

pageSections.title: Every predictor needs a deployment-time explanation

items.label: Availability
items.title: When is the value known?
items.body: A maintenance model can use signals observed before the prediction timestamp.

items.label: Derivation
items.title: How was it calculated?
items.body: Target-derived summaries and transformations using future cycles leak answer information into training.

items.label: Sequence
items.title: Which records precede the test case?
items.body: Random row splits can place later-cycle information in the training set for an earlier prediction.

items.label: Physical meaning
items.title: Why should the signal matter?
items.body: Capacity, resistance, current, time, and cycle variables need a coherent link to degradation behavior.

pageSections.caption: Refract Stats workspace for battery analysis.

pageSections.title: MAE, RMSE, and R² answer different questions
pageSections.description: The model comparison stores all three measures for each run.
pageSections.markdown:
MAE gives the average absolute prediction error in the target unit. RMSE gives larger misses more weight, which matters when a late maintenance prediction carries higher cost. R² describes variance explained relative to a constant baseline.

The score table must retain the split, target, predictors, and model settings. A metric without those fields cannot be reproduced or interpreted operationally.

pageSections.title: Select the model only after the audit passes
pageSections.description: A lower error is actionable when the split matches deployment, predictors exist at prediction time, and the comparison beats a declared baseline.
pageSections.markdown: Refract records the audit findings with the run so a result can be rejected for leakage or predictor timing even when its headline score is strong. Production maintenance performance still requires prospective data from the target equipment and operating conditions.
